name: First Reformed Church (RCUS)
denomination_detail: Reformed Church in the United States — Northern Plains Classis (Eureka Classis heritage)
pastor_credentials: RCUS ordination (Three Forms of Unity subscription required)
services: Sundays 9:00 AM worship; 10:30 AM Sunday School

score_notes.christology: Heidelberg Catechism (Q&A 29–52) and Belgic Confession (Articles 18–21) confess orthodox Trinitarian and Chalcedonian Christology.
score_notes.scripture: Belgic Confession Articles 3–7 affirm the inspiration, sufficiency, and authority of canonical Scripture as the rule of faith.
score_notes.gender: RCUS Constitution restricts the offices of minister, elder, and deacon to qualified men only — male-only ordained officers.
score_notes.leadership: Plurality of male elders (consistory) under presbyterial-classical polity (classis and synod).
score_notes.soteriology: Three Forms of Unity — monergistic regeneration, sola fide, sola gratia, sola Scriptura, particular redemption per the Canons of Dort.
score_notes.cultural: RCUS / Eureka Classis fought a successful theological and legal battle to continue as the true RCUS when the parent body merged into the Evangelical and Reformed Church in 1934 — paradigmatic confessional resistance.
score_notes.denominational: Reformed Church in the United States — German Reformed heritage tracing to Boehm's 1725 organization in Pennsylvania; the modern RCUS preserves the Eureka Classis line.
score_notes.preaching: Catechetical preaching (Heidelberg Catechism Lord's Day series) is standard RCUS practice in the second service or Sunday school.
score_notes.mens_discipleship: Family worship, catechism instruction, and male headship in home and church are emphasized in the German Reformed tradition.
score_notes.mission: RCUS supports Westminster Biblical Missions and partners with NAPARC churches in domestic and foreign missions.

assessment: First Reformed Church (RCUS) in Aberdeen, South Dakota, pastored by Rev. The congregation subscribes to the Three Forms of Unity (Heidelberg Catechism, Belgic Confession, Canons of Dort) and restricts ordained office to qualified men.
enrichment_notes: Added from RCUS Northern Plains Classis records.

name: St. Mark's Reformed Episcopal Church
denomination_detail: Reformed Episcopal Church — Diocese of the Northeast & Mid-Atlantic; founded 1873

score_notes.christology: REC affirms the historic Christian creeds and the 39 Articles — orthodox Trinitarian and Chalcedonian Christology.
score_notes.scripture: Article VI of the 39 Articles affirms Scripture's sufficiency; REC was founded explicitly to defend Reformation Anglican biblical authority.
score_notes.gender: REC restricts holy orders (bishop, priest, deacon) to qualified men only.
score_notes.leadership: Episcopal polity in apostolic succession; rector with vestry; male-only ordained orders.
score_notes.soteriology: Reformation Anglican soteriology per the 39 Articles — justification by faith alone (Article XI); REC was founded by Bishop George Cummins in 1873 specifically to preserve evangelical Reformation theology.
score_notes.cultural: REC was founded in 1873 by George David Cummins as evangelical resistance to ritualism in the Episcopal Church — paradigmatic confessional Anglican resistance.
score_notes.denominational: Reformed Episcopal Church — Diocese of the Northeast & Mid-Atlantic; now part of ACNA via REC.
score_notes.mens_discipleship: Male vestry leadership; men's ministries common.
score_notes.mission: REC partners with ACNA missions and global Anglican south.

assessment: St. Mark's Reformed Episcopal Church in Jenkintown, Pennsylvania, with Fr. Patterson serving as Rector since 2011, is a parish of the Reformed Episcopal Church's Diocese of the Northeast & Mid-Atlantic. The REC was founded in 1873 by Bishop George David Cummins as evangelical resistance to ritualism, and upholds the 39 Articles, the 1928 BCP tradition, and male-only holy orders.
enrichment_notes: Added from REC Diocese of the Northeast & Mid-Atlantic directory.
